vo_text.1: In 1949, Cal Johnson pulled a 67 pound, 8 ounce musky out of a Wisconsin lake. The IGFA lists it as the all tackle world record for the fish of ten thousand casts.
vo_text.2: Big muskies hunt by sight from cover. They lurk along cabbage weed edges, right next to deep water drop offs.
vo_text.3: To trigger a reaction strike, anglers burn double blade bucktails fast, just inches over the weed tops, where muskies hide below.
vo_text.4: Never pull your lure out early. Some pros say up to forty percent of their muskies hit right at the boat, so finish every cast with a wide, deep figure eight.
vo_text.5: Burn fast, work the turn, and you'll understand why...
